title: Chapter 1 – Role of Arbiters & Duties: Mock Exam

questions.text: How early before a round should an arbiter arrive at the playing hall for the FIRST round of a tournament?

options.text: 15 minutes
30 minutes
1 hour
2 hours

questions.explanation: Per Article 1.2, for the first round the arbiter should arrive at least one (1) hour before the start. For subsequent rounds, 30 minutes before is the minimum.

questions.text: Which of the following is an acceptable behaviour for an arbiter while supervising games in progress?

options.text: Leaving the playing area every 15 minutes to smoke
Sitting at a computer surfing the internet
Actively observing all games, especially those in time trouble
Speaking on their mobile phone in the playing hall

questions.explanation: Per Article 1.1, arbiters must observe all games, especially those in time trouble. Leaving the area frequently, surfing the internet, or using mobile phones are prohibited behaviours.

questions.text: What is the primary duty of a FIDE Arbiter?

options.text: To assist players with their strategy
To see that the Laws of Chess are strictly observed
To record all moves of each game
To broadcast the games to spectators

questions.explanation: Per Article 1.1, the arbiter shall see that the Laws of Chess are strictly observed, act in the best interest of the competition, and ensure a good playing environment.

questions.text: What is the role of the Chief Arbiter in a tournament?

options.text: To play in the tournament alongside the other participants
To oversee all other arbiters and take final responsibility for arbitral decisions
To organise accommodation and travel for players
To determine prize fund distribution only

questions.explanation: Per Article 1.5, the Chief Arbiter oversees all other arbiters, takes final responsibility for arbitral decisions, and ensures all procedures comply with FIDE regulations.

questions.text: Which of the following must an arbiter do BEFORE a round starts?

options.text: Check all equipment is in place, boards set up and clocks ready
Announce the pairings during the game
Inspect players' bags for electronic devices
Verify FIDE ratings of all players

questions.explanation: Per Article 1.3, before each round the arbiter must verify all equipment is in place, boards are correctly set up with pieces in the right starting position, and clocks are set and ready.

questions.text: An arbiter notices a player repeatedly knocking pieces off the board carelessly. What should the arbiter do?

options.text: Ignore it as this is not an arbiter's concern
Immediately forfeit the player's game
Warn the player and monitor behaviour; escalate if repeated
Ask the opponent if they are offended

questions.explanation: Per Article 1.1, the arbiter must act in the best interest of the competition. Disrupting play by carelessly knocking pieces is an infraction that deserves a warning with escalation if the behaviour continues.

questions.text: What should an arbiter do at the END of each round?

options.text: Collect scoresheets and record all results
Allow players to freely take the equipment home
Begin the next round immediately without break
Submit rating reports to FIDE automatically

questions.explanation: Per Article 1.4, after each round the arbiter must collect all scoresheets from both players, record results, and prepare for the next round including computing pairings.

questions.text: Can an arbiter refuse to implement an appeal committee decision?

options.text: Yes, if the arbiter believes the committee is wrong
No, the arbiter must implement all valid decisions of the appeals committee
Only if the Chief Arbiter agrees the decision was incorrect
Only in title norm tournaments

questions.explanation: Per Article 1.5, the arbiter must implement decisions of the appeals committee. The arbiter cannot refuse to implement a committee ruling even if they personally disagree with it.

questions.text: Which of the following is a key BEFORE-GAME duty of the arbiter?

options.text: Publishing the pairings
Collecting the prizes
Negotiating with the organiser about fees
Conducting opening ceremony speeches

questions.explanation: Per Article 1.3, before-game duties include publishing the pairings, ensuring equipment is ready, confirming venue is prepared, and verifying that clocks are correctly set.

questions.text: How should an arbiter handle a protest or complaint from a player during a game?

options.text: Dismiss it and ask the player to focus on their game
Ask the opponent what they think happened first
Listen carefully, gather facts, and make a ruling according to the Laws
Always refer it to the organiser without making any decision

questions.explanation: Per Article 1.1, the arbiter must act impartially. When a protest is made, the arbiter must listen carefully, gather all relevant facts, and make a fair ruling strictly in accordance with the Laws of Chess.
